title: Dormancy and Why Cannabis Seed Responses Vary
objective: Distinguish dormancy from quiescence, nonviability, physical restriction, and poor test conditions.

terms.definition: A living seed's failure to germinate under conditions that would otherwise support germination.
Metabolic inactivity caused by absence of a required external condition such as water or suitable temperature.
Dry storage period during which dormancy-related physiological state can change.
Mechanical or chemical influence of the fruit coat on water entry, gas exchange, or embryo expansion.

coreScience: Failure to germinate is not automatically dormancy. The unit may be dead, immature, infected, mechanically damaged, exposed to unsuitable temperature or water status, deprived of oxygen, or scored too early. Dormancy is a specific physiological state in a viable seed and requires evidence that suitable conditions were provided.

Cannabis lots vary. Maternal environment, maturation, drying, storage age, genotype, fruit-coat properties, and testing method can all change response. Research on low-germinating industrial hemp lots found that priming and pericarp removal altered germination performance, supporting the possibility that coat-related restriction and physiological state can contribute in some lots. That result does not justify routinely cutting or removing coats from production seed.

Hormonal regulation, especially the balance of abscisic acid and germination-promoting signals, interacts with metabolism and environment. These mechanisms are complex and largely derived from general seed science. The operational task is to use controlled comparison tests, not to label every delayed seed with a presumed mechanism.
cultivationRelevance: When a lot underperforms, first verify identity, temperature, moisture, oxygen, test duration, and scoring. Then compare an untreated control with any justified diagnostic treatment on a separate sample.
Reserve invasive methods such as coat removal for research, rescue, or germplasm work with appropriate skill; they can injure the embryo and bias the test.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Untreated sample conditions, observation schedule, and final categories.
Evidence for dormancy, coat restriction, immaturity, infection, or environment.
Exact treatment, sample size, control, duration, and operator.
Change in timing, final germination, abnormal seedlings, and injury.
Supported mechanism, unresolved hypothesis, or reason to reject the lot.

misconceptions: Every hard seed is dormant: Hardness by touch does not establish viability or a physiological state.
Scarification is always beneficial: Unnecessary abrasion can damage the embryo or increase infection.
One rescue treatment proves the cause: Treatment effects can have multiple mechanisms and require controls.
evidenceLimits: Cannabis-specific dormancy classification is less developed than for many model and crop species. State observations and tested responses without overstating the mechanism.
